name: rendertrail
description: Records how a React component renders in headless Chrome and explains the main performance problem in a card, with the line to change.
long_description: Claude passes in a few component files and a short interaction, such as typing into a search box. Rendertrail runs them in headless Chrome on your computer, records every React render with real timings, and shows the main problem in a card: what is wrong, what it costs, which components re-rendered for nothing, and the exact line to change. After Claude applies a fix, the same interaction runs again and the card shows before and after. Everything runs locally: the recorded page has no network access, and runs are stored in ~/.rendertrail/runs. Needs Google Chrome (or Playwright's Chromium).

tools.name: inspect_render
tools.description: Record how a React component renders while someone interacts with it, and explain the main performance problem. Use it when a React UI feels slow or re-renders too often. Pass only the files needed to render the component (replace data fetching with static data), the file to mount, and a short interaction, such as typing into an input. Returns the main problem, what it costs and the line to change. To check a fix, call it again with the changed files and `baselineRunId`.
